verdicts.why: Andre talks Lia into giving him a little of her hope, takes all of it, leaves her comatose on the roadside and drives off; nothing friendly passes between them afterwards. Under the rule, a clear betrayal turns the kind at that title.

The rules say stage 0 cannot sit on the first episode while it describes Krista as Marcus's lover and spy, since she is only turned and recruited at #2. But no source (Wikipedia, Marvel Database episode pages for #1 to #13) names the episode where they become lovers, so the stage cannot be placed under the evidence rule; the owner has to pick the episode or accept merging it into #2.

They never share a scene, but Dooley's whole case is the hunt for Howard, and in S1#7 he dies in Howard's unfinished heat vest, which Jarvis says cannot be removed. That counts as huge consequences under the exception (MCU Wiki lists Howard as Dooley's former enemy).

In Absolution Talbot works on the kill codes with Coulson and Fitz while Yo-Yo is with Mack and Lincoln at Hive's silo freeing hostages; the plot has no scene between them. Two separate actions side by side are not a stage.

value.title: X-Men: First Class
value.text: Moira brings Charles to the CIA, and they lead the mission against Shaw together. Afterward she promises to keep his school secret, but he wipes her memory.
value.on_a_card_about_b: CIA officer who works with Charles against Shaw. He wipes her memory.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Telepath who leads the mission against Shaw with Moira. Wipes her memory.

verdicts.why: The connection clearly starts in First Class: Moira takes Xavier to the CIA, they lead the mission against Shaw, and at the end he wipes her memories. A connection that starts in an earlier title gets a stage there.

Danielle is a toddler who never meets Mr. Charles; the attack targets Jessica (he tells her it was meant to make her back off), and Luke's CIA work is Luke's own deal. That is not a connection between Danielle and him, and not a huge-consequence case for her.

On screen the only crossing is Endgame's Camp Lehigh, where Howard asks Jarvis about Tony and Tony and Jarvis never interact; Jarvis caring for young Tony and the J.A.R.V.I.S. naming come from the tie-in comic. VisionQuest#4 only shows his photo in records of the AIs' human models, which is knowing about, not knowing.
N'Jobu dies long before Toussaint is born and nothing passes between them in Wakanda Forever; a blood tie never met is not a connection under the rules.

In Tablet of Time Silvermane fires Hammerhead, who sides with the Kingpin, Silvermane's opponent in the gang war; in Ravages of Time he works for the Kingpin at the exchange with Silvermane. Being fired turns the kind at that title, and they are now on opposite sides of a crime war.

Debra is listed in The Insidious Six and Morbius, but no source shows a scene between her and Morbius there; the Marvel Database lists both in flashback in The Awakening (#47), which can carry the lab-partner backstory. Not clearly sourced, so it passes.

Ward is trying to arrest Lorelei when she enthralls him, and the bond lasts only while her spell holds, until Sif takes her; she is his former thrall-master. Under the rule an enchantment doesn't make partners.

value.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3#18
value.text: Jemma and Fitz seek out Radcliffe for help against Hive, and Jemma sees through his fake-eye test. Then Daisy and Hive's followers burst in and take him.
value.on_a_card_about_b: S.H.I.E.L.D. scientist who sees through Radcliffe's fake-eye test.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Transhumanist scientist Jemma seeks out for help against Hive.

verdicts.why: They first meet in The Singularity (S3#18), where Simmons stabs his fake eye and he tests the pair before Daisy and Alisha take him; they then work together against Hive in S3#22 and on his research afterwards. The connection clearly starts at S3#18.
In Endgame Bucky and Peter only fight in the same Battle of Earth with no scene between them; a shared battle is not a stage, and the 'now' card lines are also against the rules.

The S2#4 arrest is a one-off scuffle; for the rest of the season Costa keeps Trish in protective custody at Riverbank, questions her gently and gives her his card. Their through-line until the S3#13 hunt is cooperative, not hostile.
